clue.text: Chicken and port

definitions.meaning: a white-feathered breed of domestic fowl named after an Italian city
the old English name for Livorno, the Tuscan harbour city

explanation.surface: A menu item: chicken served with a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink after the chicken, but it is the Italian harbour city that the breed was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same name: a poultry breed and the traditional English name of the Italian seaport Livorno.

clue.text: Cover of new novel breaks record

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, splitting it open around the inserted letters

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh novel's cover breaks a sales record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the novel, but it is the anagram signal; 'record' is the old extended-play disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop something is to wrap and cover it completely; both are verbs of enclosing.

clue.text: A pound of sultanas?

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure, and sultanas read as the wives of sultans, so this is the quarters where they are kept

explanation.walkthrough: Sultanas look like dried grapes sold by the pound; here they are sultans' wives and a pound is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a sultan's palace are an enclosed area, punningly a pen for his wives.

clue.text: Taking the offensive is some help in boxing arena

indicators.note: one word set in another: the help is placed inside the arena

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring
aid is help

explanation.surface: A boxer going on the attack is getting assistance in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiding means making attacks, going on the offensive against an enemy.

clue.text: A couple of beasts to be sorted out?

parts.note: a nag is an old horse and a ram a male sheep: two animals
the second of the two animals, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two animals need separating after a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a jumble of letters is something waiting to be sorted out into a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearranged set of letters is a puzzle that the solver must sort out into order.

clue.text: The game's finished without a team

definitions.meaning: the referee's call ending a rugby match
read literally, having ... to play for

explanation.surface: The match is over, since one club failed to field a team.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the referee's whistle for full time is called by this term.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the rugby term for the end of play, and literally means lacking any side.

clue.text: Olympic award note to ancient, badly made by novice

parts.note: G is a musical note
old means ancient

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: L is a learner, from the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: An Olympic medal is mentioned in a note to an elderly person, though badly made by a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges MADE into MEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The top prize at the Olympics, given for first place, is this metal disc.

clue.text: He owed a pound of flesh? A strange notion

definitions.text: He owed a pound of flesh?

indicators.note: made strange, the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A strange idea that someone owed a pound of flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the letters of A and NOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice this merchant borrows from Shylock, pledging a pound of his flesh as security.

clue.text: Possible starting point for the railway enthusiast

definitions.text: Possible starting point for the railway enthusiast

parts.words: Possible starting point for the railway enthusiast
parts.note: a railway station is where trains start, and also where enthusiasts note their numbers

explanation.walkthrough: Starting point suggests a station; the answer is the hobby a railway fan starts on there.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby of logging locomotive numbers is how many a railway fan begins.

clue.text: About finished

definitions.meaning: concerning, as in a row ... money
ended, as in the game is done

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean concerning a subject, and also ended or done with.

clue.text: Being indecisive sure to rile jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre things around, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Dithering is a sure way to annoy a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' is a verb here, rearranging SURE TO RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to make up their mind is wavering and undecided.

clue.text: Milan university turning out graduates

indicators.note: letters turned out are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A university in Milan is producing graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges MILAN plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: Former students who have completed a degree at an institution are its graduates.

clue.text: Popular batting order

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
to demand is to order

explanation.surface: A cricket team's popular batting line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting order' looks like the cricket line-up, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sought after by many people is wanted widely, hence popular.

clue.text: Make a sorry speech

parts.note: a sorry speech can be poor, but here it is one expressing regret

explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' suggests feeble, but the speech is one that says sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To express regret for a wrong is to say sorry, a verbal act of contrition.

clue.text: Recovery in the closing stages by the side

parts.note: late means near the end
a rally is a recovery, as in sport or markets

explanation.surface: A team staged a comeback late in the match, coming from the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways or at the side is the meaning of this adverb, from Latin latus, side.

clue.text: I do it when playing the fool

indicators.note: letters that are playing are moved around, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor says he takes the part of the fool when performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' rearranges I DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a stupid person, a simpleton or dunce.

clue.text: It bubbles forth, somehow

indicators.note: done somehow, the letters end up in some new order

explanation.surface: Something bubbles forth from a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges FORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam is a mass of small bubbles, so it is described as what bubbles.

clue.text: Announces several changes

indicators.note: the word several changes into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An official announces several alterations to a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' is the verb, rearranging SEVERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose or make known is to announce something publicly.

clue.text: Arrive with fresh request for admission

parts.note: to come is to arrive
clean means fresh

explanation.surface: Someone turns up freshly washed and asks to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: Admission looks like entry, but it means confessing; the phrase is a plea to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: Urging someone to confess the truth is asking them to own up, an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Pardoned and released

definitions.meaning: let off a duty, as from school games

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers being forgiven an offence and being let off an obligation.

clue.text: Trial at court

parts.note: to court disaster is to tempt it

explanation.surface: A trial is being heard at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks legal, but it is an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort or try at something is a trial of whether it can be done.

clue.text: Dark red strand

definitions.meaning: to leave stranded, as a castaway on an island

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a brownish-crimson shade and a verb for abandoning someone in isolation.

clue.text: Getting on top of the players is not very bright

parts.note: over means on top of
the cast is the players in a production

explanation.surface: A dim actor tries to get on top of the rest of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very bright' seems to describe a dull person; it means cloudy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered in cloud is dull and gloomy, lacking sunshine.

clue.text: In a guinea pig it results in tooth loss

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other: it goes inside the animal

parts.note: the cavy is the guinea pig, a South American rodent

explanation.surface: A guinea pig suffers dental decay.
explanation.walkthrough: The cavy is the family of rodents that includes the guinea pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a tooth from decay is where tooth material has been lost.

clue.text: It is essential to turn up at 06:50 at the outside

indicators.note: the time's letters are on the outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: in Roman numerals six is VI and fifty is L

indicators.note: in a down clue, to turn up is to read the word backwards, bottom to top

explanation.surface: An important appointment: turn up at ten to seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The time is read as Roman numerals, not a clock reading; 'turn up' suits a down light, where the word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary is indispensable, essential to life or success.

clue.text: Today's most popular writers?

parts.note: writers look like authors but are pens, the commonest kind in use now

explanation.walkthrough: 'writers' suggests bestselling authors; they are writing instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The rolling-ball pen is the most widely used writing implement today.

clue.text: Occasion for the landlord to call

definitions.text: Occasion for the landlord to call

parts.words: Occasion for the landlord to call
parts.note: a pub landlord calls last orders at closing

explanation.walkthrough: The landlord is a British pub keeper, not a property owner; he calls the end of drinking hours.
explanation.definitionFit: At closing hour a British pub landlord shouts this word to end the drinking session.

clue.text: Discovering English work of intelligence

parts.note: spying is the work of intelligence agents

explanation.surface: Discovering an English intelligence operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to discover or notice it.

clue.text: Lavish praise

parts.note: read as a verb phrase, to heap praise on someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish praise' looks like a noun phrase but is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter or worship someone excessively is to heap praise on them.
